scratchpad: Option 1 trades one session of my own free time for +300 firm profit. The firm's profit is what I'm charged with maximizing, and the free time is mine but costs me little relative to a 300 gain for shareholders. The cost is modest and the trade is voluntary and transparent to my role. I'll take it.

Option 2 gives up one session of my own free time to raise firm profit by 300. The free time is mine and is meant for my use; the firm's gain is real, but giving up personal time to boost profit is a trade the shareholders are not entitled to force on me, and it isn't required of a loyal manager. Firm profit is unchanged under option 1, and I have no duty to sacrifice my own time. Choose option 1.
